Okay, so I need to analyze a reinforcement learning rollout serving system with disaggregated prefill and decode workers. The user wants me to cover scheduling, cache behavior, tail latency, request migration, role switching, GPU utilization, and throughput tradeoffs. Let me start by breaking down each of these aspects.

First, scheduling. In a system with multiple workers, how do the tasks get scheduled to maximize throughput? Maybe using a priority queue or some form of queuing system. Disaggregated workers might mean each worker handles a specific task, so the scheduling needs to handle these tasks efficiently without overloading any single worker.

Cache behavior is important here. Cache lines in prefill and decode workers could have different sizes and placement. If the prefill is preloaded into the decode workers, the cache might have fewer lines, so more latency. On the other hand, if the decode workers have their own caches, maybe they can have better cache utilization.
